<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94e29cd11f5d959a4847369837ce719879497b15` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

git fetch origin 7b7b9f509a12674ad3fc6417e1f83efbc92105dd && git checkout 7b7b9f509a12674ad3fc6417e1f83efbc92105dd

## Contract review

Written at 2026-10-27T21:41Z.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Who throws, from where.** `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts:121` — `render()` throws `Error('TEMPLATE_INVALID: ' + refusal.message)` for any parsed hole carrying `refusal`. `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts:1476-1483` — `resolveAndRenderTemplate` catches exactly that prefix and rethrows as `TEMPLATE_INVALID: email template NAME (locale=ROW_LOCALE): ` + the rest. `renderTemplate` (:1497-1499) and `sendTemplate` (:1508-1509) both call that resolver first, before any transport, queue or `sys_email` row. So "from both methods", the message shape, "nothing is delivered" / "nothing is rendered" all hold. Note the locale in the message is the resolved row's locale, which the contract's `(locale=LOCALE)` placeholder covers.
2. **Throw vs return, consistent with siblings.** `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` (:1389, :1411), `TEMPLATE_INACTIVE` (:1414) and `MISSING_VARIABLES` (template-engine.ts:155, re-thrown :1428) are all thrown `Error`s with the code as message prefix, never a `{ status: 'failed', error }` return — `TEMPLATE_INVALID` is thrown the same way. The contract's existing three entries name the code without saying throw or return; the new entry says "refused at render, as TEMPLATE_INVALID: …" — same register, no new dialect. The .mdx heading "may return/throw implementation errors" is pre-existing and the new bullet fits it.
3. **The rule and its name.** `packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:45` `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_HOLE_GRAMMAR = 'email-template-hole-grammar'`; registered gating, `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['email_template']` (`authoring-rules.ts:2472-2481`). The grammar is `judgeHoleFormatter` (`packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts`): `chainsASecondFormatter` → rule `one-formatter`; `formatter === 'currency' && arg !== undefined && !/^[A-Z]{3}$/` → rule `currency-code-literal`. The contract's "a second formatter, or a `currency` argument that is not a literal ISO 4217 code" is exactly those two branches. (`currency` with NO argument is admitted and formats USD — the contract says "argument that is not", so it does not overclaim.)
4. **"Permanent" and "until re-published".** The same grammar gates `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` and the `email_template` runtime publish door (registry entry above; PR #26799 pins it at 422 `INVALID_METADATA`), so a template cannot be re-published with the hole, and nothing but a new publish changes the stored row. `service-messaging` grades it permanent on both channels (`email-channel.ts:425`, `inbox-channel.ts:254`). `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx:115-119` already states the same ("judged at its next publish; until then sendTemplate and renderTemplate fail with TEMPLATE_INVALID"). Both sentences hold.
5. **`TEMPLATE_UNSUPPORTED` left out: correct.** Repo-wide, the string is produced only by `service-messaging` `email-channel.ts:339` and `inbox-channel.ts:174`, as the CHANNEL's own `status: 'failed'` error when the registered `email` service lacks `sendTemplate` / `renderTemplate`. `plugin-email` never emits it and no `IEmailService` method can. The card's "if the contract also documents it" condition is false, so nothing to check in.
6. **Error-code ledger untouched: correct.** `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` registers "every service-specific code a route may put in `error.code`" (its header); `git grep` of `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND|TEMPLATE_INACTIVE|MISSING_VARIABLES|TEMPLATE_INVALID` over it returns 0 hits. The four codes are thrown-`Error` message prefixes from a kernel service, never a REST envelope code, so the ledger is the wrong register. The triage line's "add it to the ledger if it is not there" is answered by measurement, and the PR body says so.
7. **Other docs and skills.** `git grep` of the four codes over `skills/**`, `.claude/skills/**`, `content/docs/**`, `docs/**`, `examples/**` and plugin-email / service-messaging markdown: the only enumerations of the vocabulary are `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx` (updated here) and `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx` (already names `TEMPLATE_INVALID` at :118). `content/docs/references/system/email-template.mdx:51` is AUTO-GEN and names `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` inside the locale description, not as a list. No plugin-email README exists. The three docs-drift pages (`client-sdk.mdx`, `self-hosting.mdx`, `kernel/contracts/index.mdx`) name `IEmailService` but list no codes — nothing to update. CHANGELOGs are release-owned. The `Skills-docs:` line is true as written.
8. **Generated artifacts.** `packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts:918-919` — `contracts/` holds TypeScript interfaces, not Zod schemas, so this TSDoc feeds no `content/docs/references/**` page; `api-surface` records export names, not comments. No regeneration owed; the file list is complete.
9. **The .mdx bullet.** True sentence by sentence (see 1, 3, 4); "`renderTemplate` raises it too" is true. The page's Methods block has never listed `renderTemplate` — a pre-existing gap this PR neither widens nor owes.
10. **Verification claim.** `/compare/0ca6a3723...6978e5812` touches only the .mdx (+1), so the dev's spec test and typecheck on `0ca6a3723` cover the head's `packages/spec` tree exactly as claimed.
